S1.headline: This room can move a generator.
S1.body: The grid operator told its own board that a data center's AI training can swing its draw hard enough to reach the machines.

S2.headline: Follow the wire both ways.
S2.body: At one end a building that can swing what it draws. At the other a machine that has to take it.

S3.headline: This is one large load.
S3.body: The grid operator's own term for it. The record names no company and no county for any of them.

S4.headline: The word in the paper is fatigue.
S4.body: The grid operator says a load's swing can reach here. It does not say that it has.

S5.kicker2: Emerging operational risks posed by Large Loads
S5.headline: Three risks. Three states of repair.
S5.cite: c15 c16 c18 c19 c21 c22 c26 TEXAS AI DOCKET
S5.body: One rule in force. One at the board this month. One not written, and it carries no number.

rows.desc: Sensitive compute equipment trips offline during normal grid events, leading to grid imbalance and instability.
rows.mit: NOGRR 282 / NPRR 1308. Ride-through requirements for Large Computational Loads.
rows.status: The PUCT approved NOGRR 282/ NPRR 1308 in July, effective on August 1.

rows.desc: Certain data centers processes can oscillate in a way that damages grid equipment.
rows.mit: Draft NOGRR. Large Load processes must not oscillate in a manner that would cause damage.
rows.status: ERCOT plans to submit NOGRR in September or October.

rows.desc: Dynamic models for Large Loads have proven to be inaccurate and thus are inadequate for studying their grid impacts.
rows.mit: PGRR 144, model quality rules. Texas A&M is developing more accurate models.
rows.status: TAC endorsed PGRR 144 in August and is up for Board consideration in September.

S6.kicker2: The third row of the table
S6.headline: One model is finished. The other is not.
S6.cite: c22 c23 c25 TEXAS AI DOCKET
S6.body: The grid operator says its models of these loads have proven inaccurate, and that Texas A&M is building better ones. The crypto model is released. The data center model is still being written.

S7.headline: The limit is drawn. The load is not.
S7.cite: c29 c34 c21 TEXAS AI DOCKET
S7.body: The grid operator's draft rule would hold a large load's swing to this. It has not been filed and it carries no number.

S8.kicker: What the presentation does not name
S8.headline: Every county in Texas. Not one of them named.
S8.body: The presentation names no data center, no company and no generator. Texas A&M is the only institution in it besides the grid operator and the commission.

S9.headline: The rule to watch has a page.
S9.cite: c21 c26 c37 c3 TEXAS AI DOCKET
S9.body: The model rule reached the board this month. The swing rule has not been filed, and the grid operator gives September or October. Both are tracked at texasaidocket.com.
